title: Takotsubo Cardiomyopathy with Cardiogenic Shock: Improvement with Intra-Aortic Balloon Pump Support in a 72-Year-Old Female
content:
Background: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy (TC) can mimic acute myocardial infarction, presenting with similar symptoms and ST-segment elevation on ECG but often without obstructive coronary artery disease.
Case Summary: A 72-year-old female presented with chest pain, ST-segment elevation, and elevated troponin levels suggestive of acute coronary syndrome (ACS). Cardiac catheterization revealed mild non-obstructive coronary artery disease. She developed cardiogenic shock and hypoxemic respiratory failure, necessitating mechanical ventilation and circulatory support with an intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP). Her ejection fraction improved from 5-10% on admission to 35% by discharge.
Discussion: This case underscores the importance of differentiating TC from ACS and highlights the potential role of IABP in supporting severe TC with cardiogenic shock. IABP may stabilize hemodynamics by decreasing afterload and enhancing coronary perfusion, allowing myocardial recovery in select cases of TC.
Take-Home Messages:
Mechanical support with IABP can play a crucial role in managing cardiogenic shock in Takotsubo cardiomyopathy, helping bridge patients to recovery.
Compared to the Impella device, IABP offers a lower-cost option with fewer complications, particularly reduced rates of hemolysis, vascular injury, and bleeding.
